candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items); related activity statement: prioritize delivery of client care based on acuity.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Prioritization of client care based on acuity within Management of Care
candidate.educational_objective: Prioritize nursing care according to client acuity, addressing acute clinical deterioration before routine care for stable clients.

options.A: Assess and respond first to the client with an acute change in neurologic status before completing routine care for stable clients
options.B: Complete scheduled routine tasks in room-number order regardless of changes in client acuity
options.C: Delay reassessment of an acutely changing client until all stable clients have received routine hygiene care
options.D: Use the same priority for every assigned client because acuity should not affect care sequencing

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan defines Management of Care as providing and directing nursing care that protects clients and the care environment. Its related activity statements explicitly include prioritizing the delivery of client care based on acuity and organizing workload to manage time effectively. An acute neurologic change represents a higher-acuity need than routine stable care, so reassessment and response take priority. B, C, and D intentionally ignore acuity-based prioritization. The final item tests a core RN management function rather than a vague list of tasks performed by a neuro-ICU nurse.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current official NCSBN test plan directly supports acuity-based prioritization as an RN Management of Care activity.
candidate.source_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan → Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care.
